Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Painful, cracked, itchy skin on palms for 3–4 months, worse recently, interfering with work.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Onset: began approximately 3–4 months ago after switching jobs.
  - Course/progression: gradually worsened; past few days prevented from working (off work past 3 days).
  - Symptoms: dryness, cracking of skin on palms, intermittent itch, occasional bleeding after scratching; reports milder dryness elsewhere (legs).
  - Exposures: works as a hotel housekeeper; frequently uses bathroom cleaning products and reports inconsistent glove use.
  - Treatments tried: E45 emollient (no improvement); oral antihistamine (no benefit).
  - Response expectation/advice given: advised to wear gloves, use stronger emollients 3–4 times daily, prescribed topical steroid (prescription to be sent to pharmacy); return if no improvement in 10–14 days or sooner if worsening/spreading.
- Past medical history:
  - Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  - No known prior skin diagnoses.
- Medications:
  - Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Previously tried E45 emollient and an antihistamine (no details on antihistamine dose/route/frequency).
- Social history:
  - Occupation: hotel housekeeper (cleans bedrooms, bathrooms, corridors).
  - Gloves: not consistently worn at work.
  - Tobacco: denies smoking.
  - Alcohol: a couple of pints per week.
- Allergies:
  - None reported.

- No objective imaging or laboratory results available.

   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Contact dermatitis
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Irritant contact dermatitis
     - Allergic contact dermatitis
   - Investigations planned:

   - Treatment planned:

     - Stronger emollients recommended to apply 3–4 times daily.
     - Avoidance measures: wear protective gloves when cleaning; avoid identified cleaning-product exposures.
     - Follow-up: review in 1–2 weeks (10–14 days); return earlier if symptoms worsen or spread.
